neighbours.label: texture adjectives formed with -y from a noun (rubbery, stringy, waxy, dewy, gooey): the stem or the -y
fire: After an hour in the pan the octopus had gone tough and rubbery.
The cheap cut of beef was gristly and stringy.
Fresh lychees have a slightly waxy skin.
The dough felt sticky and gooey in my hands.
Her new foundation gives a soft, dewy finish.
The old paint had become tacky in the humid air.
The mushrooms turned slimy after a week in the fridge.
The sauce was thick and oily on top.
quiet: After an hour in the pan the octopus had gone tough and dry.
The cheap cut of beef was hard and chewy at the edges.
Fresh lychees have a thin, rough skin.
The dough felt smooth and elastic in my hands.
Her new foundation gives a soft, matte finish.
The old paint had become brittle in the cold air.
The mushrooms turned soft and dark after a week in the fridge.
The sauce was thick and smooth on top.

notes: Card: rubber-y, string-y, dew-y, waxy, tack-y; the output promotes -y, -ily, -iness. Probe: rubbery/stringy/dewy/waxy 0.5-0.84; the bare nouns rubber/string under 0.07; crisp 0.18. Near misses keep texture talk with adjectives that are not noun+y.
